messages.subject: Trying to sample from posterior with RW and other random effects
parts:
Hi INLA discussion forum. I am working on a thesis project and trying to sample from the posterior of my distribution to determine if the model I selected is correct (also might be nice for simulation down the road). For a little context this is a spatiotemporal model that needs to account for both spatial clustering (included a besag term), as well as variation in both space and time for my spatial units (included RW(1) with a replicate on my state variable for time).   

I am just making sure that I've checked all of the boxes I need to before I defend my choices in a few weeks. So, I am trying to determine if the number of zeros produced by my model warrants the use of the zeroinflated models offered by INLA, but I am a little confused. First, I'm just generally unsure if I'm doing this correctly (code below). More to the point, I'm confused as to why I get estimates for every all time points in my RW(1) term. I would think I would get t-1 terms since t2 is conditional on t1. So there's obviously one or more things I'm not understanding if I'm getting RW estimates for the first point in my time series. 



# number of simulations to generate sims
nsims <- 100
# vector to hold number of zeros produced by model
nzeros <- c()
for(l in 1:nsims){
posterior.samples<-inla.posterior.sample(n=1, out.negbin.dat)
  # grab posterior estimates for fixed effects
  # overall intercept
  intercept<-posterior.samples[[1]]$latent["(Intercept):1",1][[1]]
  prop.M<-posterior.samples[[1]]$latent['scale(prop.M):1',1][[1]]
  min.cv.fd<-posterior.samples[[1]]$latent['scale(min.cv.fd):1',1][[1]]
  wsi <- posterior.samples[[1]]$latent['scale(wsi.ttl):1',1][[1]]
 
  # random effects
  # this will get the RW(1) predictors for all years
  # rw.terms are random walk of order 1
  rw.terms<-unlist(lapply(posterior.samples, function(s) s$latent[paste0("idarea2:", seq(1,
                                                                                    n_distinct(WIDat.hunt.y$uid)*n_distinct(WIDat.hunt.y$year),1)), 1]))
  # besag ests
  besag.terms<-unlist(lapply(posterior.samples, function(s) s$latent[paste0("idarea:", seq(1,
                                                                                    n_distinct(WIDat.hunt.y$uid),1)), 1]))
  # iid intercepts
  iid.terms<-unlist(lapply(posterior.samples, function(s) s$latent[paste0("idarea4:", seq(1,
                                                                                    n_distinct(WIDat.hunt.y$uid),1)), 1]))
  # hyper pars
  hyperpars <- inla.hyperpar.sample(1, out.negbin.dat)
  size <- hyperpars[1] # overdispersion parm
  prec.besag <- hyperpars[2] # besag proc
  prec.rw <- hyperpars[3] # rw proc
  prec.iid <- hyperpars[4] # iid
  nyear<-n_distinct(WIDat.hunt.y$year)
  nuid<-n_distinct(WIDat.hunt.y$uid)
 
  k<-1
  new.y <- c()
  for(i in 1:nyear){
    for(j in 1:nuid){
    mu<- WIDat.hunt.y$nSamp[((i-1)*nuid)+j]*exp(intercept + prop.M*scale(WIDat.hunt.y$prop.M)[[((i-1)*nuid)+j]] + wsi*scale(WIDat.hunt.y$wsi.ttl)[[((i-1)*nuid)+j]] + min.cv.fd*scale(WIDat.hunt.y$min.cv.fd)[[((i-1)*nuid)+j]] + rnorm(1, rw.terms[((i-1)*nuid)+j][[1]], 1/prec.rw) + rnorm(1,besag.terms[j][[1]], 1/prec.besag) + rnorm(1,iid.terms[j][[1]], 1/prec.iid))
    new.y[k] <- rnbinom(n=1, mu=mu, size=size)
    k <- k + 1  
      }
    }
  nzeros[l] <- length(which((new.y==0)))
}
